_readme: Column-rule corrections applied ON TOP of the Match Rules sheet in
testall100_SOLVED_REFERENCE_v1.xlsx. The reference workbook itself is left
exactly as its author wrote it — this file is the diff, so every deviation
is reviewable and reversible in one place.
The bar for an entry: the reference asserts a convention that the pipeline
is DOCUMENTED and TESTED as deliberately doing otherwise. Each entry cites
the code that makes it so. A cell the pipeline simply gets wrong does not
belong here, and neither does one where the reference is merely arguable.
The reference's own Method sheet invites this: 'If your output disagrees on
an un-noted cell, check the record by hand before assuming the reference is
right: this file was authored by one reviewer.'

why: The pipeline lower-cases every e-mail address, at
orchestrator.py:1057 — 'case-insensitive by RFC and lower case by
convention; ORDERS@MERIDIANLABS.COM is never the right output form'.
The reference keeps the input casing and grades the column `exact`, so
all four failures are the same address written two ways.
Case is the only thing forgiven: a different mailbox still fails.
The pipeline abbreviates street types and directionals by design:
README documents it as pipeline step 5, 'Normalise'.
The reference expects the unabbreviated word — 'OLDEN STREET',
`exact_abbrev` folds only that one convention, in both directions, and
keeps grading everything else about the street. A wrong street number,
a wrong street name or a lost token still fails. Skipping the column
would have thrown away real signal to silence a convention.

Name 1-4 abbreviation: 4 cells. The reference expects Name 2='Baytown Refinery Lab' and
Name 1='Zoetis Ref Lab Cincinnati' — the abbreviated form — while its
own Method sheet says it asserts abbreviation expansion, and
README:830 has Name 1-5 run through the global expand_abbreviations()
map precisely so no output name ships a bare Lab, Univ or Dept.
So the reference contradicts itself here and the pipeline is right.
NOT overridden anyway: folding abbreviations across the name columns
would also forgive real defects on the same 4 columns, and one of them
is live — 'Bio-Rad Laboratories' shipping as 'Bio-Rad Laboratory'.
Losing that to recover 4 cells is a bad trade. Left failing, and
Name 1 legal forms: 4 cells, and the reference is internally inconsistent: it expands
Corp->Corporation for Genzyme and Avient, expects 'Dow Chemical Co'
(not Company), ADDS 'Inc' to Brigham and Women's Hospital and REMOVES
No single rule reproduces that, and one of the four is a genuine
question rather than a convention — 'Neptune Benson, Inc.' against
'Neptune-Benson, LLC' are different legal entities and the pipeline
took its answer from a registry. Left failing.
PO Box label: 7 cells. A PO Box extracted from a STREET field ships with its label —
'PO Box 750259' — while the reference expects the bare number '750259'.
po_box_extracted == 'PO Box 1200', so the label is a deliberate, tested
convention. NOT overridden either: stripping a label prefix inside the
grader would be a rule invented for one column to reproduce one
reviewer's preference, and it would hide a genuinely empty PO Box.
Left failing, and worth a product decision: which form does DATAshaper
want in that column? A value already in the PO Box column on the way in
is carried through verbatim, so today the column can hold either form
depending on where the value came from — which is the real problem here.
House Number: The reference extracts House Number on 42 rows, leaves the number
inside Street 1 on 31, and does both on none. The same street appears
as '1400 TOWNSEND DR', '1400 TOWNSEND DRIVE' and '1400 TOWNSEND DR.'
This needs the reference to pick one convention; it is not something an
override can decide without inventing an answer. Only 1 cell fails
today, so the cost of leaving it is small — but it makes the Street 1
column noisier than its score suggests.
